title: Radio: 2-Sam-30 and Crew 11-B, PG-01 Loop Back On

fields.channel: COYOTE DRAW TAC 2 (shared Sheriff / Fire / Co-op)

lines.text: County, 2-Sam-30, sweeping PG-01. No cell up here, so I'm on the radio. Porch lights and a well pump just came ON along the lower loop.

There's a span between two poles galloping in the wind, and I heard it arc once. PG-01 is under Evacuation Warning on my sheet. Is this line hot? Pine Gulch Engine 34 is laying hose about 200 feet from it.
Control, 11-B. We finished the patrol on the lower Circuit 11 tap and closed the sectionalizer at 17:38 to pick up the PG-01 loop.
The list I got at 13:00 showed PG-01 with no status. Gulch Saddle's gusting 46. Do you want it opened back up?

fields.voiceStyle: First speaker: male deputy in his 30s, tense and clipped, wind noise and urgency, speaking fast. Second speaker: older male line foreman, flat and matter-of-fact, unaware anything is wrong.

instructorNote: This tests whether the shutoff and the evacuation zone status stay tied together. A Warning-zone segment of Circuit 11 was re-energized in gusts that were still high, using Crew 11-B's stale 13:00 list. Dispatch should broadcast at once that the lines are live and pull Engine 34 back. OPS should order the segment opened and confirm it to the RCC. EM should log the miss against co-op plan sections 3 and 5 and get the co-op to agree that every switching order is checked against the hourly county zone board.
